alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun and the phrasal particle that completes *lay up* (rules 17 and 44).

`תּוּשִׁיָּה` rendered *sound wisdom*. The subtraction test ties, so the ASV's own use decides: it writes a bare *wisdom* for `חׇכְמָה` in this same chapter, which makes *wisdom* the class noun and *sound* the specifier, so the head stays on *wisdom* (rule 31). The competing reading heads on *sound*, as `בָּמָה` → *high place* does.
Substantival adjective keeps its own word; the article beside it holds the *the*.

Referential subject pronoun answering to no morpheme in this verbless clause; `added` under rule 20, which keeps only the presentative dummy with the predicate. The ASV italic corroborates and decides nothing (rule 7).
Nominal predicate of a verbless clause; the construction-supplied copula joins it (rule 20) and the indefinite article belongs to the nominal expression (rule 15).
Anarthrous participle used substantivally; the supplied *them that* joins its unit and the head is the word carrying the lexeme (rule 46).
Nomen rectum takes the construct relation, here recast as *in* (rule 19).

review_notes: The marginal note *Or, And a shield for etc.* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
The variant unit selected the base reading and covers s001, which is aligned as ordinary source text (rule 9).
The supplied *He* is `added` while the supplied *is* joins the nominal predicate — the two supplied words do different offices and are not one run (rules 2 and 20).
